correctness.rationale: Exact differentiation yields d(y+z)/dt=y(y+b) and trace DF=2y. For b≠0, rho=exp[-2(y+z)/b] has weighted divergence -2 y² rho/b, hence an exact positive finite-time weighted Jacobian. For b<0, if any forward-bounded radius set had positive volume, strict expansion under time-T map would contradict its forward invariance and finite weighted volume. At b=0, monotone P and omega/alpha limit invariance imply only the origin is a bounded complete trajectory; every bounded forward trajectory converges to it. Integrating dP/dt against any compact stationary state produces the variance parabola, and endpoint rigidity follows from constant-y invariant trajectories. Polynomial checker verifies all differential identities at the final artifact path; no finite simulation is promoted to an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural diagnostic in the original case-P literature is which (a,b) regions exhibit observable bounded chaotic, periodic or stable dynamics rather than unbounded motion. The theorem proves that for every a the entire negative-b half-plane has no positive-volume basin of bounded forward solutions, gives exact critical-b recurrence collapse, and identifies strict positive-b weighted contraction. This is a global, sharp sign boundary and a usable stationary moment/phase-volume constraint, not simply restating a pointwise Jacobian or enumerating arbitrary parameters. The equilibria show why an almost-everywhere formulation is mathematically necessary.
